title: Philippines Charitable Giving Assistance Act
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on March 24, 2014. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Philippines Charitable Giving Assistance Act - Treats cash contributions made after the enactment of this Act and before April 15, 2014, for the relief of victims in areas affected by Typhoon Haiyan as having been made on December 31, 2013, for purposes of the tax deduction for charitable contributions. Deems such a contribution as meeting the recordkeeping requirements of the Internal Revenue Code if the taxpayer produces a telephone bill showing the name of the donee organization and the date and amount of the contribution.

summary.headline: A 2014 law lets people who gave cash to Typhoon Haiyan relief in early 2014 claim the donation as if they gave it in 2013, and lets a phone bill serve as proof.
summary.what_it_does: For cash gifts made after the law was enacted and before April 15, 2014, to help victims of Typhoon Haiyan, the law treats the gift as made on December 31, 2013, for the charitable deduction. This means the donation can count toward a 2013 tax return. The law also says a phone bill showing the charity's name, the date, and the amount meets the Internal Revenue Code's recordkeeping rules for these gifts.

who_it_affects.group: Taxpayers who gave cash to Typhoon Haiyan relief between March 25 and April 15, 2014
who_it_affects.how: They can treat those gifts as 2013 contributions when claiming the charitable deduction.

who_it_affects.group: Taxpayers who itemize deductions and gave cash to these relief efforts
who_it_affects.how: They can use a phone bill showing the charity's name, date, and amount as proof instead of other standard receipts.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was enacted on March 25, 2014. Its special treatment applies to cash gifts made from that date through April 15, 2014.
